correctness.rationale: For z=β exp(−r), f′=(z−c)f and f″=[(z−c)²−z]f. The larger curvature root is B(c) and the smaller is below c, giving strict concavity on the rising branch if c<β≤B(c) (including strict interior concavity at threshold). For β>B(c), N(r)=rf′(r)−f(r)+f(0) has derivative rf″(r); it grows from zero to its positive inflection-point value and decreases to f(0)−f(r*)<0 at the mode. This proves the unique positive tangent on (0,r*). The 0-to-t support line contacts f only at 0,t, and the envelope then follows the strictly concave increasing branch before joining the horizontal plateau. The Jensen bound for every finite-first-moment law is sharp: the chord's contact set forces the stated weights, including collapse to the unique point mass at t, and an interior strict-branch tangent forces a point mass. The unique pointwise maximizer forces attainment only by its point mass at the modal mean; larger exact means can approach the supremum with mass (m−r*)/(M−r*) at M→∞, but not attain it. The same argument with mode 0 gives Case I. A nondegenerate mixture requires strictly β>B(c) and 0<m<t. Inspected the finite-grid script and its limits. A separate example calculation gave t≈0.63299296892124, mixture value ≈0.03615418508760 and deterministic value ≈0.03455499616969; the proof, not this check, establishes global uniqueness and nonattainment.

value.rationale: The two independent hazards give a simple benchmark for a natural question: can heterogeneity improve expected establishment at the same transport budget? The answer is a sharp parameter/mean classification with the whole optimizer, not an arbitrary profitable two-point example. The nonattainment regime also identifies a meaningful difference between an exact mean and a mean cap or bounded habitat. Value is mathematical in the stipulated model; no empirical or evolutionary prediction is inferred.
